about: Self-contained rewrites of tests/fixtures/quality/bad_exercises.json, written to CONTENT_SPEC Q1–Q8. The quality checker must report none of them. `_rewrites` is a note for people.

exercises.q: A query on a Delta table with 200 columns selects 3 of them and filters `WHERE order_date = '2026-01-05'`. Which statement assigns the two savings correctly?
options: Reading only 3 columns is column pruning; skipping files whose date range cannot match is data skipping
Reading only 3 columns is data skipping; skipping files is column pruning
Both savings come from column pruning, because the filter is on a column
Neither: Delta always reads every file and drops rows in memory
why: Right: pruning removes columns, skipping removes whole files or regions.
Swapped: this is exactly the confusion to avoid.
A filter on a column does not remove columns; it lets the engine skip files whose statistics exclude the value.
Delta keeps per-file min/max statistics precisely so that it does not have to read every file.
exercises.explain: Column pruning reduces **which columns** are read, so it helps whenever a query needs few of many columns. Data skipping (with partition or clustering pruning) reduces **which files** are opened, using the min/max statistics of each file. The tempting swap mixes up the two axes: columns are the width of the table, files are its length.

exercises.q: A folder holds plain Parquet files, with no table format on top. Which of these does it **not** give you by itself?
options: Atomic commits: a write of ten files is seen completely or not at all
A history of versions you can query or restore
A consistent snapshot for a reader while a writer is adding files
Min/max statistics per column in each file
why: Missing: a reader can see some of the ten files before the others land.
Missing: there is no log of versions, only the files that exist now.
Present: this is what Parquet as a columnar format does.
Missing: without a transaction log a reader may list a half-written folder.
Present: Parquet footers carry per-column statistics.
exercises.explain: Parquet describes how data sits **inside each file**: columns, encodings, compression, statistics. Everything about the **set of files as a table** — atomic commits, versions, consistent snapshots under concurrent writes — needs a transaction log, which is what Delta Lake adds on top. The tempting picks are compression and statistics, but those live inside the file and Parquet already has them.

exercises.q: On Databricks, `CREATE TABLE sales (id INT, amount DOUBLE)` with no `USING` clause creates a Delta table.
exercises.explain: Delta Lake is the default table format on Databricks, so a `CREATE TABLE` without `USING` makes a Delta table. You need `USING PARQUET` (or another format) to get anything else. The trap is to assume that no `USING` means plain files.

exercises.q: In `abfss://data@company.dfs.core.windows.net/orders/`, which part is the **storage account**?
why: This is the scheme (ABFS over TLS).
This is the container: it comes before the `@`.
Right: the storage account is the first label after the `@`.
This is part of the Data Lake Storage endpoint host.
exercises.explain: An ADLS Gen2 URI reads `scheme://container@account.dfs.core.windows.net/path`. The container sits **before** the `@` and the account right **after** it. Swapping the two is the usual mistake, because in most URLs the first name is the bigger thing.

exercises.q: Table `orders(order_id, customer_id, amount)`. Write a query that returns the total `amount` per customer.
exercises.explain: `SUM(amount)` aggregates and `GROUP BY customer_id` makes one row per customer. Every selected column that is not aggregated must appear in `GROUP BY`; leaving it out is the classic error.

exercises.q: A nightly job rewrites a folder of **plain Parquet** files (no Delta) while an analyst's query is reading it. What can the analyst's query return?
options: A mix of old and new files, or an error for a file that vanished mid-read
Always the complete old data, because Parquet files are immutable
Always the complete new data, because the reader waits for the writer
Nothing: Spark refuses to read a folder that is being written
why: Right: with no transaction log there is no snapshot to read, only whatever files exist at each moment.
Each file is immutable, but the set of files is not, and that set is what the reader lists.
There is no lock or commit protocol in plain Parquet for the reader to wait on.
Spark has no way to know a plain folder is being written.
exercises.explain: Without a table format, a 'table' is just the files a listing finds, so a concurrent rewrite can expose a half-old, half-new state or a missing file. Delta's log fixes this by giving every reader one committed version. The tempting answer confuses immutable **files** with an immutable **table**.
